criteria.criterion: The root cause of the mismatch between the Athena-Job trailer and the closing records in commit 64ecdc9 is identified in the change description, and the code path that produced it is fixed.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. D63's 'Root cause' is marked 'an inference from the code, since the history is not available to the change'. It explains only why the commit was accepted: the binary that landed it predated the rule. It never says how the landing path came to pair the trailer `20261010-132713-ezm8` with the records of `20261010-131714-adcd`, for example through retry_landing, a nested run, or concurrent jobs. No producing code path in run.rs or manage.rs changes. The only change on the production side is the new history check.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`. A new regression test reproduces a landing whose Athena-Job trailer names a different job from the closing records it adds, and shows the in-process gate refuses it or the landing path can no longer produce it.
criteria.evidence: `landing_tests::a_landing_whose_trailer_names_another_job_than_its_records_is_refused` stages HONEST's records with trailer `Athena-Job: 20261010-132713-ezm8`. It asserts that the invariant reports 'the Athena-Job trailer names 20261010-132713-ezm8' and that check_landing reports violations. The test passed. It pins down behaviour the gate already had rather than a new fix.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run --locked -- check --history` from the repository root. It reports no violation for 64ecdc9 and exits 0. Any exemption or handling of that commit is explained in a code or doc comment.
criteria.evidence: The cited command fails with exit 101: 'could not determine which binary to run'. With `--bin athena` it exits 2 and reports violations for b2a5b4c and 144d225. This verify repo holds only the two synthetic commits, and 64ecdc9 is absent, so the claim can't be shown here. The exemption is explained in the comments on `LEGACY_MISMATCHED_LANDING` and in D63, and a predicate unit test covers it, but no run of the real history exits 0.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`. A new test shows that a change to the gate (crates/athena-gate) which makes the full-history check fail cannot reach a verified landing, because the landing path runs the history check on the resulting tree or tip and refuses.
criteria.evidence: The new tests pass, but each one builds a history that already fails because of an unlabeled hand change: `a_verified_job_does_not_land_while_the_history_check_fails`, `a_landing_on_a_history_that_fails_the_check_is_refused`, and `the_landing_time_history_check_refuses_...`. None lands a change to gate code. The mechanism calls `athena_gate::history::check_landing` from the running binary. D63 says 'a candidate that changes crates/athena-gate is judged by the old gate until the next landing ... It is not a proof that the candidate's own gate accepts the history', and M30 says the same. So a gate change that makes the history check fail can still land as verified.

criteria.criterion: docs/enforcement.md (and CHANGELOG.md if it records behavior changes) name the new mechanism with its refusal and allowing tests. Any change to athena.toml is listed as a deliverable and named in a criterion.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. enforcement.md adds an M30 row with refusal tests and allowing tests, and CHANGELOG has Fixed and Changed entries. athena.toml is unchanged, and D63 says so. The policy test `every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists` passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`. Both are clean, and `cargo test --locked` passes.
criteria.evidence: fmt produced no output. clippy finished with no warnings. Every test suite reported ok with 0 failures; only the ignored live and helper tests did not run.

findings.summary: Landing-time history check uses the running binary's gate, so a gate change that breaks the history check can still land as verified (the reported failure mode).
findings.evidence: `require_clean_history` calls the compiled-in `athena_gate::history::check_landing`. D63 says: 'a candidate that changes crates/athena-gate is judged by the old gate until the next landing ... It is not a proof that the candidate's own gate accepts the history.' The user asked to 'make sure a gate change can't land as verified while the full-history check fails'.

findings.summary: Root cause not established and the producing code path not fixed.
findings.evidence: Labelled 'an inference from the code'. It explains acceptance by an older binary, not why a landing built for one job carried another job's closing records. No change to build_commit, retry_landing, or the code that composes trailers or records.

findings.summary: The `check --history` acceptance command can't be run as written, and 64ecdc9 handling is unverified against the real commit.
findings.evidence: `cargo run --locked -- check --history` gives 'could not determine which binary to run'. The `--bin athena` form exits 2 on this two-commit tree. The exemption is tested only on a synthetic id `64ecdc9000…` through the predicate.

findings.summary: The exemption matches a 7-hex-character (28-bit) commit id prefix, so the claim that 'a commit id cannot be chosen in advance' is weak.
findings.evidence: `id.starts_with("64ecdc9")`. A 28-bit prefix can be brute-forced. The full commit id would pin it exactly, and the full id is available once the commit is in history.

request_reading_mismatch: The reading is right. The candidate drifted from it on two points. First, it never looked into why the landing path built a commit whose trailer names one job while its records belong to another; it only explains why the gate let that commit through. Second, it reads "a gate change can't land as verified" as "the running binary's gate re-checks history at landing time". That still lets a gate change land as verified when the change itself is what breaks the history check, which is exactly the reported incident.
summary: The change adds a history check that runs before each landing (`history::check_landing`, without the gitleaks scan) to `land_or_block` and `retry_landing`. It also accepts commit 64ecdc9 by name, and adds tests, a D63 entry, an M30 enforcement row and a CHANGELOG entry. I ran fmt, clippy and `cargo test --locked`; all pass, including the 5 new tests. The verdict is still fail, for three reasons. (1) The root cause is labelled "an inference from the code". It explains why the gate accepted the mismatch (an older binary was running) but not which code path wrote ezm8's trailer onto adcd's records, and that path is not fixed. (2) The new check runs the running binary's gate, not the candidate's. D63 and M30 both admit it "is not a proof that a candidate's own gate code accepts the history". So a gate change that makes `check --history` fail can still land as verified, which is what the user asked to prevent. The tests only cover histories that already fail (hand changes), not a gate change. (3) Criterion 3 can't be shown here. The cited command fails because `cargo run` can't choose a binary. With `--bin athena` it exits 2, because this verify tree has only two synthetic commits and 64ecdc9 is not in it. The exemption is checked only by a unit test of the predicate on a made-up commit id.
